doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining Basie and life on the road
title: Basie pay, raises, family and arranging fees
summary: He started at $150 a week, reached about $200, doubled in Europe, and relied on $35-50 arrangements and royalties.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: We’ve talked about the traveling situation. How was pay?

Pay must have been pretty good for the veterans, the guys, Marshall Royal and Henry Coker and Joe Newman and Renauld Jones and Freddie Green, of course. To me, one who had not been a professional, but fresh out of the army -- I don’t consider that a professional musician life. New in the industry, $150 a week was adequate, and I

got two raises. Once I got a $10 raise after a few years, to $160 a week. Then I got another raise to $175 a week. When I left the orchestra in ’64, I think I was making about $200 a week. One benefit was that whenever we went to Europe, salaries were doubled. In other words, while I was making $150 a week in the States, on a European tour the salary was doubled to $300.
Of course dollars meant something different in 1955 or ’56 than they do now.
Right, right, exactly. Brower:; One wouldn’t want $150 a day now.
You could do a lot when you could do -- did you have a family at that point?
I was married in June of 1954.
Did you have children is what I mean.

I didn’t have -- my first-born didn’t arrive until December of 1957, so I went for roughly four-and-a-half years without a family, without children. I was just a year in the band before getting married. Then in ’59 my second child was born. I think it was about that time I got the second raise.

So were you able -- one way of gauging the meaning of those dollars that you made was at that time, given your family responsibilities, were you able to maintain yourself without any kind of undue strain on that?

Not adequately, no. The only thing that helped bail me out was income from arranging. At that time I was making from $35 to $50 per arrangement. And royalties from recordings, which were very minimal, but still they helped a lot.
So you’re saying if you -- I think I’ve seen the figure. 150 arrangements you did for the Basie band.
That figure is not necessarily accurate. I don’t know how many I wrote. I would say close to 100, between 100 and maybe 120.
